title: Balanced counterexamples to Ryser's conjecture at prime orders
main_claim: For every sufficiently large prime q there is an intersecting (q+1)-partite (q+1)-uniform hypergraph with exactly q+1 nonisolated vertices in each part and covering number q+1. This disproves Ryser's conjecture tau <= (r-1)nu, even in the balanced intersecting case. The hypergraph is built from AG(2,q) by merging two parallel lines and splitting two others into opposite pairs of 4-point sets in every direction.

issues.location: deletion.tex, Lemma prime-stability (citation of Szonyi-Weiner Thm 4 / Heger-Nagy Result 3.6)
issues.description: The concentration-of-core-covers step depends entirely on the quoted prime-plane stability theorem: |B| <= 3(q+1)/2 - beta and Delta < (2/9)(beta+1)^2 imply a line with at least q - 2Delta/(q+1) points of B. I checked the constant bookkeeping (Delta <= 0.0201 q^2 < 2q^2/81 < (2/9)(beta+1)^2 with beta = floor(q/3), q >= 100) and it is correct. I did not compare the hypotheses and conclusion against the original source. Any discrepancy there, for example a different skew-line threshold or a conclusion stated as |B| - ... rather than q - ..., would propagate into the result.
issues.evidence: If q is prime and B has |B|<=3/2(q+1)-beta, Delta<2/9(beta+1)^2 ... then some projective line contains at least q-2Delta/(q+1) points of B.

coverage:
I read all of paper.tex, construction.tex, deletion.tex, candidates.tex, selection.tex, local.tex and elementary.tex.

Checked in detail:
- The deterministic reduction (Prop. 2.1): partition and part sizes, intersection via the 4-cycle of merged pairs, and injectivity of edges.
- The cover argument: reduction to a line cover of R_0, t <= rho*q/4, the parallel-pencil case (8 designated points against 3 remaining labels, each covering at most 2, using compatibility condition 3), and the affine case (forcing q+1-b labels through occupancy on R_0 and R, including the M_g^1 case with the 1+B+2t bound). The b=0, 1, 2 and >=3 sub-cases also check.
- The profile-counting lemma: the mark-probability upper bound from the affine second-moment identity (re-derived), the lower bound on P(N >= m + xi*q/2), and the witness-count cancellation q^m.
- The three deletion applications (Poisson factorization; the c=1, P_01=mu argument).
- The Szonyi-Weiner constant arithmetic.
- In selection: the equal-survival drift for domains and degrees, the exceptional-set censoring, the hazard barrier, the occupancy drift B_*T/q, the LLL weights and conditional cylinder bound, and the exp(O(q)) domination ratio computation.
- In candidates: E H_g ~ 16q (independence of the 8 offsets), the Cauchy-Schwarz distinct-line count, and the degree and codegree sources.
- In local.tex: the extension table for kappa >= 3, the aligned-law factor q^{-4b} (offset disjointness checked), the surplus count 2b+2-2kappa, the acyclic 3-colouring extraction, and the four-event reduction for kappa=2.

Spot-checked rather than fully re-derived: the moment-lemma conditional counts (a)-(d) in candidates.tex.
